title: R2: orchestrator/capacity.py — global capacity snapshot and deterministic admission with critical-path reservation only against present demand (AP P6)
spec:
Why: daemon.free_slots (orchestrator/daemon.py:449-465) reduces capacity to one integer; waves then ignore per-task executor eligibility (complexity range, cooling, daily task budget, Claude worker headroom, account utilization) and premium capacity can be spent on low-impact work while a critical-path task waits (AP P6; brief P3).
What: new pure module orchestrator/capacity.py; no daemon edits (integration is a later task).
- snapshot(pool, running_claude=0, inflight_claude=0) -> {"executors": {id: {"free": max_parallel-running, "cooling_s", "enabled", "roles", "complexity": [min, max], "day_tasks_left": daily_budget_tasks-day_tasks or None, "weight"}}, "claude_workers_free": limits.max_parallel_claude_workers - running_claude - inflight_claude, "accounts": {id: {"utilization": acct.utilization(window_cap), "cooling_s"}}, "fallback": bool(all enabled execute executors cooling)}. Read fields from pool.Executor/Account (orchestrator/pool.py:68-145, 522-536); never mutate the pool.
- eligible_executors_from_snapshot(task, snapshot) -> executor ids with role execute, enabled, not cooling, complexity in range, free > 0, day_tasks_left None or > 0.
- admit(ranked_ids, tasks, snapshot, priorities, durations=None, cfg=None) -> {"admit": [ids in rank order], "deferred": {id: reason}, "assignments": {id: executor_id}, "reasons": {id: text}}. Greedy in rank order: pick the eligible executor with most free then lowest weight; decrement free. Reservation rule (deterministic, present demand only): if task X is eligible on exactly the executors that a higher-ranked still-unassigned ready task Y needs and admitting X leaves Y with zero capacity this tick, defer X with reason reserved_for_critical naming Y. Never defer when no higher-ranked task competes (no speculative reservation). Reasons vocabulary: executor_capacity, cooldown, account_capacity, budget, reserved_for_critical:<id>, no_eligible_executor. In fallback mode capacity is claude_workers_free and every task is eligible when pool.fallback_tier(complexity) is not None.
- priorities: {task_id: critical_path.explain dict} (priority key used for ordering ties).
acceptance: tests/test_capacity.py::test_executor_full_defers_with_executor_capacity_reason — every eligible executor at max_parallel yields deferred reason executor_capacity
tests/test_capacity.py::test_quota_cooling_executor_is_not_eligible — a cooling executor is excluded and a task only it could run is deferred with reason cooldown
tests/test_capacity.py::test_account_fallback_uses_claude_worker_headroom — fallback snapshot admits at most claude_workers_free tasks and defers the rest with account_capacity

tests/test_capacity.py::test_critical_path_contention_reserves_for_higher_priority — a low-priority task whose only eligible executor is the last free slot the higher-ranked task needs is deferred with reserved_for_critical naming that task

tests/test_capacity.py::test_idle_capacity_admits_everything_and_no_unnecessary_reservation — with spare capacity every ready task is admitted and no reserved_for_critical reason appears when no higher-ranked task competes

constraints.interface_contract: snapshot(pool, running_claude=0, inflight_claude=0) -> dict as specified; admit(ranked_ids, tasks, snapshot, priorities, durations=None, cfg=None) -> {admit, deferred, assignments, reasons}; reason vocabulary executor_capacity|cooldown|account_capacity|budget|reserved_for_critical:<id>|no_eligible_executor; module must not import daemon

result.summary: superseded by R2 v2 after spec review T-0566 request_changes: snapshot must not call Account.utilization (mutating rollover) and must compare Executor.day to today read-only instead of trusting day_tasks; v2 adds day-boundary and non-mutation tests

spec_review_risks.issue: snapshot()'s accounts entry is specced as acct.utilization(window_cap), but Account.utilization (orchestrator/pool.py:85-94) is mutating: it resets window_tokens/planner_window_tokens on window rollover and day_tokens/planner_day_tokens on day rollover as a side effect of being called. That directly violates the spec's own 'never mutate the pool' constraint for this module. Since capacity.py is meant to be a pure snapshot taken every daemon tick, calling this on every tick means whichever code path calls snapshot() first each window/day silently zeroes real usage counters that other code (tally_planner, pool.save()) still depends on. Needs a non-mutating read of the same value (e.g. a pure helper or inlined equivalent of utilization's math) instead of calling the existing method.

day_tasks_left is specced as a raw read: daily_budget_tasks-day_tasks (or None). Executor.day_tasks is only rolled over by Executor.roll_day() (orchestrator/pool.py:134-137), which today is invoked only inside Pool.eligible_executors (pool.py:530, mutating) and at actual dispatch time in executor.py:290 -- never inside daemon.py, which has no roll_day/eligible_executors call at all. capacity.py's snapshot() bypasses both call sites, so right after local midnight, before any task has dispatched on a given executor, ex.day still holds yesterday's date and ex.day_tasks still holds yesterday's count. snapshot() would then compute day_tasks_left against a stale count (e.g. an executor that hit daily_budget_tasks=5 yesterday reports day_tasks_left=0 today instead of 5), spuriously excluding it via eligible_executors_from_snapshot. None of the five acceptance tests exercise a day boundary, so this ships green. snapshot() needs to check ex.day against today (read-only, same comparison roll_day uses) and treat day_tasks as 0 when the date doesn't match, without mutating the Executor.
